exercises.title: First bad version with n up to 2³¹ − 1 — at most 32 questions
exercises.problemHtml:
Versions 1…n were released; from some version on, every version is bad. The only way to learn anything is Api.isBad(v) (given), which counts your calls and throws if v is not in 1…n. Complete static int solve(int n) in FirstBad: return the first bad version, using at most 32 calls even for n = 2147483647.

The grader prints the answer and whether you stayed within 32 calls. The classic trap: (lo + hi) / 2 overflows to a negative number when both are near 2³¹ — isBad then throws.

Run the grader on your machine

The website does NOT grade this exercise. Press Tải .zip (download) above the code, unzip it, edit the code in src/, then inside the exercise folder (the one with cham.mjs) run:

node cham.mjs

The zip unpacks into a folder named after the exercise (<folder> below). Windows (PowerShell): cd "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\<folder>" — cmd: cd /d %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\<folder> — then node cham.mjs. macOS (Terminal): cd ~/Downloads/<folder> then node cham.mjs. Tip: type cd and drag the folder into the terminal window. You need Node.js 18+ and JDK 8 or newer (17 or 21 recommended) — javac -version must work.

The grader compiles src/ with javac, runs 3 case(s) (1 hidden — not printed in this text), compares your output line by line (trailing spaces and Windows/macOS line endings ignored), prints a diff of the wrong lines and gives a score. When it prints ALL CHECKS PASSED, come back and press Tự đánh dấu đã giải (self-mark as solved). node cham.mjs --case 2 --show prints the input and your whole output for case 2.

Requirements

  • At most 32 calls of isBad for any n ≤ 2³¹ − 1 (this is the complexity check).
  • Never call isBad outside 1…n.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Các phiên bản 1…n đã phát hành; từ một phiên bản nào đó trở đi, mọi phiên bản đều lỗi. Cách duy nhất để biết là Api.isBad(v) (cho sẵn) — hàm này đếm số lần gọi và ném lỗi nếu v không thuộc 1…n. Hoàn thiện solve(n) trong FirstBad: trả phiên bản lỗi đầu tiên, gọi không quá 32 lần kể cả khi n = 2147483647.

Máy chấm in đáp án và việc bạn có giữ trong 32 lần gọi không. Bẫy kinh điển: (lo + hi) / 2 tràn thành số âm khi cả hai gần 2³¹ — lúc đó isBad ném lỗi.

Chạy máy chấm trên máy bạn

Website KHÔNG chấm bài này. Bấm Tải .zip ở khung code, giải nén, sửa code trong src/, rồi trong thư mục bài (thư mục chứa cham.mjs) chạy:

node cham.mjs

Giải nén ra một thư mục mang tên bài (gọi là <thư-mục>). Windows (PowerShell): cd "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\<thư-mục>" — cmd: cd /d %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\<thư-mục> — rồi node cham.mjs. macOS (Terminal): cd ~/Downloads/<thư-mục> rồi node cham.mjs. Mẹo: gõ cd rồi kéo thư mục vào cửa sổ terminal. Cần Node.js 18+ và JDK 8 trở lên (khuyên 17 hoặc 21) — javac -version phải chạy được.

Máy chấm biên dịch src/ bằng javac, chạy 3 ca (1 ca ẩn — không in trong đề), so output từng dòng (bỏ qua khoảng trắng cuối dòng và kiểu xuống dòng Windows/macOS), in diff dòng sai rồi cho điểm. In ALL CHECKS PASSED ⇒ quay lại đây bấm Tự đánh dấu đã giải. node cham.mjs --case 2 --show in input và toàn bộ output của bạn cho ca 2.

Yêu cầu

  • Không quá 32 lần gọi isBad với mọi n ≤ 2³¹ − 1 (đây là phép kiểm độ phức tạp).
  • Không bao giờ gọi isBad ngoài 1…n.

exercises.title: The single element in a sorted array of pairs — O(log n) with a parity invariant
concepts: binary search without a target value
exercises.problemHtml:
a is sorted and every value appears exactly twice, except one value that appears once. Complete static int single(int[] a) in O(log n). XOR of all elements or a linear scan is O(n) — correct, but the complexity check calls your method 200,000 times on a million elements.

Key observation: before the lonely element every pair starts at an even index (a[2i] == a[2i+1]); after it, every pair starts at an odd index.

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 1,000,001 elements × 200,000 calls) inside a 3-second limit. An O(log n) per call solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an O(n) per call (XOR / linear scan) one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

Run the grader on your machine

The website does NOT grade this exercise. Press Tải .zip (download) above the code, unzip it, edit the code in src/, then inside the exercise folder (the one with cham.mjs) run:

node cham.mjs

The zip unpacks into a folder named after the exercise (<folder> below). Windows (PowerShell): cd "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\<folder>" — cmd: cd /d %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\<folder> — then node cham.mjs. macOS (Terminal): cd ~/Downloads/<folder> then node cham.mjs. Tip: type cd and drag the folder into the terminal window. You need Node.js 18+ and JDK 8 or newer (17 or 21 recommended) — javac -version must work.

The grader compiles src/ with javac, runs 3 case(s) (2 hidden — not printed in this text), compares your output line by line (trailing spaces and Windows/macOS line endings ignored), prints a diff of the wrong lines and gives a score. When it prints ALL CHECKS PASSED, come back and press Tự đánh dấu đã giải (self-mark as solved). node cham.mjs --case 2 --show prints the input and your whole output for case 2.

Requirements
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
a đã sắp và mọi giá trị xuất hiện đúng hai lần, trừ một giá trị xuất hiện một lần. Hoàn thiện single(a) trong O(log n). XOR mọi phần tử hay quét tuyến tính là O(n) — đúng, nhưng kiểm độ phức tạp gọi hàm của bạn 200.000 lần trên một triệu phần tử.

Nhận xét then chốt: trước phần tử lẻ loi, mọi cặp bắt đầu ở chỉ số chẵn (a[2i] == a[2i+1]); sau nó, mọi cặp bắt đầu ở chỉ số lẻ.

⏱ Kiểm độ phức tạp. Một ca chạy code của bạn với input LỚN (n = 1,000,001 elements × 200,000 calls) trong hạn 3 giây. Lời giải O(log n) per call xong trong chưa tới một giây trên laptop bình thường; bản O(n) per call (XOR / linear scan) cần lâu hơn rất nhiều và ca in TOO SLOW. Hạn đặt rộng có chủ ý — trượt ca này thì do thuật toán, không phải do máy bạn.

exercises.title: The k-th missing positive number — binary search on a computed value
exercises.problemHtml:
a is a strictly increasing array of positive ints. Complete static int kthMissing(int[] a, int k): the k-th positive integer that is NOT in a. Example: a = {3,4,8,9,12} misses 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 13 … — k = 1 → 1, k = 4 → 6, k = 10 → 15.

Before a[i] exactly a[i] − (i + 1) numbers are missing, and that count never decreases — find the first index where it reaches k in O(log n).

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 1,000,000 elements × 200,000 queries) inside a 3-second limit. An O(log n) per query solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an O(n) or O(n + k) per query one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

The website does NOT grade this exercise. Press Tải .zip (download) above the code, unzip it, edit the code in src/, then inside the exercise folder (the one with cham.mjs) run:

The zip unpacks into a folder named after the exercise (<folder> below). Windows (PowerShell): cd "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\<folder>" — cmd: cd /d %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\<folder> — then node cham.mjs. macOS (Terminal): cd ~/Downloads/<folder> then node cham.mjs. The grader compiles src/ with javac, runs 3 case(s) (2 hidden — not printed in this text), compares your output line by line (trailing spaces and Windows/macOS line endings ignored), prints a diff of the wrong lines and gives a score. When it prints ALL CHECKS PASSED, come back and press Tự đánh dấu đã giải (self-mark as solved). node cham.mjs --case 2 --show prints the input and your whole output for case 2.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: missing(i) = a[i] − (i + 1) is non-decreasing because a is strictly increasing, so "missing(i) ≥ k" is F…F T…T. With lo = the first T, the numbers 1…lo + k contain lo elements of a and k missing ones, so the k-th missing is lo + k. O(log n).

exercises.title: Minimum days to make m bouquets — binary search on the answer (first T)
exercises.problemHtml:
Flower i blooms on day bloom[i]. A bouquet needs k adjacent bloomed flowers, and each flower is used once. Complete static int minDays(int[] bloom, int m, int k): the first day on which m bouquets can be made, or -1 if impossible (m·k flowers are more than there are — careful, m * k can overflow an int).

Example bloom = {6,2,9,3,3,8,1,5}, k = 2: m = 2 → day 5, m = 3 → day 6, m = 5 → -1.

If day d is enough, every later day is too — so "enough by day d" is F…F T…T over days. Count bouquets for one day in O(n), and binary search the day between the smallest and largest bloom day.

exercises.title: Maximise the minimum distance — search on the answer for the LAST T
exercises.problemHtml:
pos holds n positions (unsorted, duplicates allowed). Place c items on c of them so that the smallest distance between two neighbouring items is as large as possible. Complete static int maxMinDistance(int[] pos, int c) (2 ≤ c ≤ n) — return that distance; do not change pos.

Example {9,1,17,4,12,20}: c = 2 → 19 (1 and 20), c = 3 → 8 (1, 9, 17), c = 4 → 3 (for instance 1, 4, 9, 12 or 1, 9, 12, 17… the best smallest gap is 3).

"Can place c items at distance ≥ d" is T…T F…F in d (greedy: take the first position, then every position ≥ d after the last taken one). Find the last T — round mid up, otherwise lo = mid loops forever.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: Feasibility is monotone the other way round (T…T F…F), so the answer is the last T. With lo = mid in the T branch, mid must be rounded up so that the interval always shrinks. Cost: O(n log n) to sort + O(n) per probe × log₂(range) probes.

exercises.title: Median of two sorted arrays in O(log min(m, n)) — binary search on a split point
concepts: partition: i elements of a, half − i of b on the left
exercises.problemHtml:
Complete static double median(int[] a, int[] b): the median of all m + n elements (both arrays sorted, m + n ≥ 1, one may be empty). For an even total it is the average of the two middle values — compute it with long: {MAX} + {MAX} must give 2.147483647E9.

Required: O(log min(m, n)) — merging is O(m + n) and fails the complexity check (two arrays of a million, 300,000 calls). Idea: choose i elements of the shorter array a and j = (m + n + 1)/2 − i of b for the left half; the split is right when a[i−1] ≤ b[j] and b[j−1] ≤ a[i] (missing neighbours count as −∞/+∞). Binary search i.

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 2 × 1,000,000 elements, 300,000 calls) inside a 3-second limit. An O(log min(m, n)) per call solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an O(m + n) per call (merging) one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

Hoàn thiện median(a, b): trung vị của cả m + n phần tử (hai mảng đã sắp, m + n ≥ 1, một mảng có thể rỗng). Tổng chẵn thì là trung bình hai giá trị giữa — tính bằng long: {MAX} + {MAX} phải ra 2.147483647E9.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: Every candidate split i of a forces j in b; "aL > bR" means i is too big, "bL > aR" means too small — a binary search over 0…m, so O(log min(m, n)). It is the classic hard interview problem precisely because the search is not over values but over split positions.
exercises.solutionExplanationHtmlVi: Mỗi điểm chia i của a buộc j của b; "aL > bR" nghĩa là i quá lớn, "bL > aR" là quá nhỏ — tìm nhị phân trên 0…m, nên O(log min(m, n)). Đây là bài phỏng vấn khó kinh điển chính vì phép tìm không chạy trên giá trị mà trên vị trí chia.

mistakesJson.loi: (leftMax + rightMin) / 2.0 with ints — two values near 2³¹ overflow before the division.|||(leftMax + rightMin) / 2.0 bằng int — hai giá trị gần 2³¹ tràn trước khi chia.
Searching the longer array — j = half − i becomes negative or larger than n.|||Tìm trên mảng dài hơn — j = half − i thành âm hoặc lớn hơn n.
